I'm 78 this year, and I've been farming these 5 mu for 40 years. My son and daughter-in-law work at the tile factory in town, so most days it's just me and the old woman in the field. We can't work like we used to — my back aches, and she can't lift heavy bags anymore. But we know this land. Every mu of it.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th, same as always. I saved some seed from last year but it's not enough, so I'll buy Jinmai from the seed shop — about 25 yuan per mu. I hire Old Zhang's small tractor to plow after the maize comes off, then we broadcast the seed and rake it in. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — about 30 kg — and then at Qingming, when the wheat is jointing, I spread another 15 kg of urea per mu if it looks yellow. The extension fellow says I could use more, but fertilizer is dear and we need money for blood pressure medicine. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Each time the pump costs about 30 yuan per mu. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu, and if the weather is normal I expect the same — around 400 kg per mu.

The maize window is always too tight. Harvest wheat around June 10th, plant maize within three or four days. I buy hybrid seed every year — saved seed doesn't work well for maize — about 45 yuan per mu. Old Zhang comes with the tractor to cultivate and plant in one go. I put all the fertilizer down at planting: 25 kg of compound and 10 kg of urea per mu. I'm too old to be chasing the field for topdressing in July heat. For water, I'll irrigate once at tasseling time if it hasn't rained. The summer rain usually helps, so maybe once is enough. I spray herbicide once, and if I see corn borer I add insecticide. For maize I expect about 1,000 jin per mu — 500 kg — same as last year if things go right.

Labor is tight. My son can only help for wheat harvest and maize planting when the factory gives him leave. The rest is me, my wife, and hired hands. I pay about 150 yuan per day for hired labor, and Old Zhang charges about 50 yuan per mu for tractor work.

Everything costs money. Seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, hired help — it all adds up to about 3,000 yuan for the year. That's a lot for us old folks. But if I don't spend it, we don't eat. So I do what I always do: not too much, not too little, just enough to get by.
